purpose: Addressable graph records for concepts already referenced by the atlas tree and relationship layers. Registry records are intentionally substantive: every registered endpoint has a human-readable definition so an atlas click never lands on an unexplained label.

records.name: Growth
records.description: Increase or transformation through time. In the atlas, growth can be biological, organizational, economic, technological, symbolic or relational and should be measured according to the relevant domain.

records.name: Life
records.description: The condition and processes associated with living systems, including persistence, reproduction, metabolism, adaptation, development and renewal. In Potatoism it also functions as a central symbolic category.

records.name: Research
records.description: The organized process of gathering, evaluating, comparing and documenting evidence, sources, methods, calculations and interpretations. Research records should preserve uncertainty rather than hide it.

records.name: Dao De Jing
records.description: Classical Chinese philosophical text traditionally associated with Laozi and foundational to Daoist thought. The atlas uses it as a comparative textual source for ideas such as Dao, non-forcing, simplicity and the vessel/way imagery without equating Daoism with Potatoism.

records.name: Poetic Edda
records.description: Collection of Old Norse mythological and heroic poems preserved principally in the medieval Codex Regius tradition. It is a comparative source for world-tree, cosmological and mythic structures, especially Yggdrasil.

records.name: Messianic Traditions
records.description: Comparative field covering messianic expectations and figures across Jewish, Christian and other historical traditions. The archive keeps distinct the traditions' own claims, texts, historical settings and later interpretations.

records.name: Christian Bible
records.description: The Christian scriptural collection, comprising the Old Testament/Hebrew Bible as received in Christian traditions and the New Testament. Exact canon, translation and interpretation vary by denomination and should be specified in research records.

records.name: Torah / Tanakh
records.description: The Jewish scriptural corpus, with the Torah as its foundational five-book section and Tanakh referring to the Hebrew Bible as a whole. The archive treats Jewish textual context independently before drawing Christian or Potatoverse comparisons.

records.name: Tim Dooley
records.description: Project-level mythic and symbolic figure around which the Tim Dooley / Potato of Life narrative is organized. This record belongs to the project's interpretive architecture and is not evidence of supernatural or political authority.

records.name: Spiritual Domain
records.description: Project-defined symbolic domain for spiritual, transcendent and metaphysical language. Claims in this domain are classified as framework, interpretation, comparative material or evidence where appropriate rather than being treated as empirical fact by default.

records.name: Acts of Thomas
records.description: Early Christian apocryphal text associated with the Thomas tradition, containing narratives, hymns and ascetic themes. It provides historical-textual context for studying the name Thomas without assuming identity with the project's Son figure.

records.name: Gospel of Thomas
records.description: Early Christian sayings collection preserved in a Coptic manuscript at Nag Hammadi, with Greek fragments also known. It is a primary comparative source for research into Thomas traditions and early Christian diversity.

records.name: Son Transformation Cycle
records.description: Project-defined sequence connecting Son, death, crucifixion, transformation, Door and Ladder imagery. It is a Potatoverse narrative structure and should remain clearly separated from claims about historical Christian events.

records.name: North Pole Christmas Myth
records.description: Potatoverse-specific symbolic geography joining Christmas, the North Pole, the Son transformation sequence and the North Axis. It is a project mythology record, not a claim about the historical location of Jesus's crucifixion.

records.name: Potatoverse Epistemology
records.description: The project's method for separating observed facts, historical claims, calculations, interpretations, mythology, hypotheses and creative material while still allowing them to be connected in a graph.

records.name: Thomas / Son Study
records.description: Comparative research topic examining the project's Son/Twin/Thomas vocabulary against historical Thomas traditions, Christian texts, apocrypha and later interpretations. Similarity is recorded as comparison, not proof of identity.

records.name: Thomas Textual Corpus
records.description: Collection of textual material relevant to Thomas traditions, including the Gospel of Thomas, Acts of Thomas and associated historical scholarship. The corpus supports source-by-source comparison of the project's Thomas motif.

records.name: Entanglement
records.description: Atlas framework for structured relationships: coupling, dependency, distance, direction, feedback, temporal order, topology and trajectory. It is distinct from quantum entanglement unless a record explicitly concerns the physical phenomenon.

records.name: Axis Topology
records.description: Project-defined model for describing Axis terrain and structural positions using Mountain, Plane, Mud, Swamp, Roots, Drain, Door and directional coordinates. It is a symbolic analytical vocabulary rather than literal physics.

records.name: Hawkins Scale
records.description: David R. Hawkins' Map of Consciousness, represented in the atlas as a historical interpretive model. Its numerical levels are not Hertz measurements and are not treated as established scientific units.

records.name: Trajectory
records.description: Ordered change through time from an initial condition toward one or more outcomes. A trajectory record can preserve turning points, alternative paths, constraints and uncertainty.

records.name: Path Dependence
records.description: Condition in which historical choices, inherited institutions or prior states alter the costs and possibilities of later choices. The concept is useful for studying why similar systems can diverge.

records.name: Threshold
records.description: Boundary or critical condition at which a system changes state, behavior or trajectory. Thresholds may be quantitative, institutional, physical, biological, social or symbolic.

records.name: Phase Transition
records.description: A qualitative change between system states or regimes. In the atlas the term is used analytically and should not be assumed to mean a thermodynamic phase transition unless the physical context warrants it.

records.name: Connection
records.description: A generic relationship between two records. Stronger relationship types such as ownership, membership, supply, causation, comparison or symbolic association should be preferred when evidence supports them.

records.name: Coupling
records.description: Degree to which change in one system or node is linked to change in another. Coupling may be physical, institutional, economic, technological, social or symbolic and should be evidenced or explicitly classified.

records.name: Flow
records.description: Movement of something through a relationship or network, such as money, energy, goods, people, information, materials or attention. Flow records should specify direction and, where possible, quantity and time.

records.name: Feedback
records.description: A loop in which an output or consequence returns to influence the process that produced it. The atlas distinguishes reinforcing and balancing feedback where the evidence allows.

records.name: Cycle
records.description: A recurring closed path or sequence in a system. Cycles can be biological, economic, institutional, historical, computational or symbolic and may be stable, amplifying or degrading.

records.name: Networks
records.description: Sets of nodes joined by relationships. Network analysis can identify hubs, bridges, bottlenecks, communities, centrality, dependency and alternative paths.

records.name: Dependencies
records.description: Relationships in which the capacity or operation of one node depends on another node, input, service, institution or infrastructure. Dependency strength and substitutability should be recorded when known.

records.name: Topology
records.description: Structural arrangement of connected components and pathways. In the atlas this includes adjacency, bridges, bottlenecks, cycles, boundaries, basins and attractor-like structures without requiring geometric distance.

records.name: System Phases
records.description: Named states or regimes through which a process can move. Phase definitions should be domain-specific and connected to observations, transitions and outcomes where possible.

records.name: Outcome
records.description: Observed or modelled result of a trajectory or intervention. Outcomes should distinguish actual results from forecasts, scenarios and hypothetical counterfactuals.

records.name: Plane
records.description: Horizontal field in the project's Axis vocabulary: the observable world where geography, bodies, people, institutions, technology, infrastructure, money and history interact.

records.name: Swamp
records.description: Project-defined metaphor for dense relational entanglement, feedback, stagnation, hidden crossings and accumulated dysfunction. It is an analytical symbol, not a claim about a literal geographic swamp.

records.name: Mud
records.description: Project-defined ground/substrate metaphor for material conditions, buried history, friction and emergence. In Potatoism it is the ordinary substrate from which the Potato rises.

records.name: Drain
records.description: Project-defined pattern in which energy, resources, attention, money or meaning continuously leave a system without equivalent renewal. Empirical uses require measurable flows or documented mechanisms.

records.name: Roots
records.description: Project-defined metaphor for hidden dependencies, ancestry, memory, historical substrate and foundational inputs. In the empirical graph, root-like relationships should be translated into specific dependency or historical edges.

records.name: Emotion and State
records.description: Comparative research domain covering emotion, appraisal, arousal, action tendencies, physiology, neural correlates, psychological states and transitions. The Hawkins model is studied alongside this evidence rather than substituted for it.

records.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum
records.description: Range of electromagnetic radiation described by frequency, wavelength and photon energy. The atlas keeps this physical measurement system separate from Hawkins' consciousness numbers and symbolic colour mappings.
